Brandon McDaniel <Brandon.McDaniel@parkview.com>:
Hello Amin or Omid, We got on our study (ID 3867) this morning to check Avicenna data quality and all of the participants show Last Recorded Data Time of Dec 31, 1969 19:00! What is happening? This is an ongoing study, so this has us very worried that something has happened to all of our study data. Did our data get deleted? Is there a way to recover the data? We also have participants in the middle of the study, so if there is something going on this then this would be destroying our study integrity and data collection at the moment. What about all our participants who are currently enrolled in the study and we were collecting data on them? Thank you for your assistance. Brandon T. McDaniel, PhD Parkview Health | Senior Research Scientist Health Services & Informatics Research Mirro Center for Research & Innovation 10622 Parkview Plaza Drive, Fort Wayne, IN 46845 Office Phone: 260.266.7247 Website: Parkview Research------

Sara Farnya:
Support Ticket: #23982------

Brandon McDaniel <Brandon.McDaniel@parkview.com>:
Thank you Sara. We also have many participants that are currently utilizing the Avicenna app and in the middle of their data collection (e.g., 3 days in to their 6 days of data collection at a certain study wave, etc.), so we are truly hoping that this issue has not affected their ongoing data collection. And we have more participants who are starting their data collection periods tomorrow, Wed, Thu, and Fri of this week. I do not know if this is the issue, but we had been in the process of contracting and payment with Avicenna, and during this time we had been allowed to utilize the “trial” study version. We had also been promised that it would be easy to transition this “trial” study into being a “real” study version without any data loss or interruption to service/data collection. Did something happen with this transition? Or did something happen in terms of some automatic data lock or automatic study stop/deletion in the background on the servers due to the study currently being set in the “trial” license version? It may not be this at all. I just didn’t know if having this information would be helpful to your team as you search for the issue. We truly appreciate your assistance with this! Thank you, Brandon T.
